title: Centered square from first-level Fourier data
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, and let $x$ be a point of that cube. Form the linear function whose coefficient at coordinate $i$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at the singleton set $\{i\}$. Its centered square at $x$ equals the square of the degree-one part of $f$ at $x$ minus the total squared Fourier weight at degree one.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
$x$ is a point of the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
